- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is high, lower the forecast by 3–8% to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., >+5% from recent peak) should be capped at +3% to prevent overcorrection.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >+10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward by 2–5% unless sentiment supports continuation.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently 2–4% below forecast, reduce next forecast by 1–3% to align with recent underperformance.  
- If sentiment is rising (increasing over last 3 days) and forecast is flat or falling, adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect momentum.  
- Avoid forecasting >+10% above 18-day high unless sentiment is >0.8 and recent volatility is high.
